DEFECT #8 — strongest evidence yet for this meta-bug.

After the fetcher split (PR #368) unblocked the 1000-issue ceiling, the next dry-run reconciler pass (run 26434693640, main @ b2119ca043) immediately hits a different crash:

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: apply() list-of-Mutation legacy batch path
currently supports outbound mutations only; got 2050 inbound Mutation(s).
Inbound dispatch should route through reconcile._dispatch_mutation /
_apply_typed per-mutation.
```

This is the fail-closed guard from PR #364 (bug 1788) firing as designed — but the deeper signal is that the production code path has NO INBOUND-MUTATION DISPATCH IMPLEMENTED AT ALL. Specifically:

- `applier._apply_typed` exists (applier.py:619) — per-mutation dispatch for typed Mutations
- `reconcile._dispatch_mutation` exists (reconcile.py:84) — direction-aware routing
- BUT `applier.apply(mutations, pass_id, repo_root)` — the entry point reconcile.reconcile_once calls — has no code to:
  1. Detect inbound Mutations in the list
  2. Route them through `_apply_typed` / `_dispatch_mutation` per-mutation
  3. Keep outbound Mutations on the batch path

In production, with no local mirror, EVERY one of the 2,050 Jira issues becomes an inbound "create-locally" Mutation. There is no code path that processes them. The reconciler cannot do its primary job (sync Jira → local mirror).

This is the meta-bug thesis fully validated:
  - Epic 4047 closed P1=PASS
  - Story DDs were structurally satisfied (unit tests pass, code paths exist, modules load)
  - But the load-bearing integration was never end-to-end validated
  - The first live operator run reveals an unimplemented critical execution path

Corpus of chain defects extended:
  - #1 (5be7) repo_root None — code defect
  - #2 (96c5) git worktree advisory lock collision — code defect
  - #3 (bbf0) missing git identity — workflow defect
  - #4 (5b1c) sys.modules dual-key dataclass — code defect
  - #5 (ec9a) fetcher alert_store import — code defect
  - #6 (1788) applier.apply(list[Mutation]) crash — code defect
  - #7 (f6cc fetcher.JQL ceiling) — hardcoded constant defect (this meta-bug)
  - #8 (current) inbound-mutation dispatch unimplemented — UNFINISHED FEATURE
  - Meta (f6cc, this ticket) — planning/implementation/verification process defect

The shift from "chain of code defects" to "unimplemented feature" is the meta-signal. Each prior defect (#1-#6, #8) is a symptom of the same root cause: the epic was treated as feature-complete based on structural-satisfaction of story DDs, without any LIVE-VERIFIED success criterion enforced before closure.
